newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIAN IMPORTS DOMINATE COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIAN IMPORTS DOMINATE COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Seven English counties can assemble between them a batting lineup formidable enough to test the Australian tourists.
Unfortunately for the England selectors, each of them is an Australian.
Australian imports dominate the county scene this season from David Boon with Durham in the north to Stuart Law with Essex in the south.
Boon, the phlegmatic Tasmanian who shored up the Australian top-order batting for a decade, has taken on possibly the most difficult task of his distinguished career.
Durham won just one match in all competitions last year and were not flattered by their last place finishes in both the county championship and the Sunday league.
"If I help Durham win a county championship in the next five years, I will be happy," Boon said.
Another Tasmanian, all-rounder Shaun Young, has the unenviable task of replacing West Indies' captain Courtney Walsh in the Gloucestershire side.
Young, who toured England with Young Australia in 1995, has been voted Tasmania's player of the year for the past three Sheffield Shield seasons.
Western Australian Tom Moody will captain Worcestershire again, Victoria's Dean Jones is in charge once more at Derbyshire while two left-handers will make their county debuts.
Yorkshire, whose plans to hire Michael Slater were scuppered when the New South Wales' opener won back his place in the Australian side, have plumped for South Australian Darren Lehmann.
And Hampshire have opted for Queensland opener Matthew Hayden, who scored 1,150 first class runs for Australia on the 1993 Ashes tour without playing a test match.
Kent have made an imaginative choice in Zimbabwean leg-spinner Paul Strang, who took 10 wickets in the drawn two-test series against England late last year.
"Back home I would play only five or six first class matches in a season outside the test matches," Strang said.
"With Kent, I will probably play about 20, so that would be a great learning experience."
Three Pakistani pace bowlers, once a rare breed, will feature in the championship.
Waqar Younis adds potency to the Glamorgan attack while Mohammad Akram takes over from West Indian Curtly Ambrose at Northampton.
Most interest will centre on Mohammad Zahid, who replaces the injured New Zealand all-rounder Chris Cairns at Nottinghamshire.
Zahid's test career opened in spectacular fashion with seven for 66 and 11 wickets in the match against New Zealand at Rawalpindi last November.
